tagline: Three summits and one small town on the range's edge.
intro: From US 6 at Warm Springs, SR 375 swings around the foot of the Reveille Range into Railroad Valley, then climbs over Queen City Summit, at 5,935 feet the highest point on the road. Down in Sand Spring Valley lies Rachel. Past it the road tops Coyote Summit, runs down Tikaboo Valley and crosses Hancock Summit to end at Crystal Springs, 98 miles on.

Much of the way it follows the northern edge of the Nellis Air Force Range, with Area 51 not far off. Travelers kept reporting UFOs, so in 1996 the state named it the Extraterrestrial Highway, and stars of Independence Day came to Rachel for the dedication.

moments.title: Rachel
moments.text: Named in 1978 for the first baby born in the valley, the town of about 50 keeps a time capsule from the makers of Independence Day, meant to be opened in 2050.

moments.title: Mail Box Road
moments.text: A lone mailbox once marked this dirt road toward the lands around Area 51 and drew UFO watchers, until its owner took it away because of vandalism.

moments.title: Crystal Springs
moments.text: The ghost town at the south end is little more than a junction and a few trees, though for a year in the 1860s it was the seat of Lincoln County.
